raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On SM100/SM103 (B200, B300), `FlashInferMLAAttnBackend` always builds its ragged (MHA) prefill wrapper with `backend="cutlass"`. FlashInfer's SM100 CUTLASS FMHA only has kernels for head dims (64, 64), (128, 128) and (192, 128). Any MLA model with other dims crashes on its first prefill.

GLM-4.7-Flash is one example: `qk_nope_head_dim + qk_rope_head_dim = 192 + 64 = 256` and `v_head_dim = 256`. With `--attention-backend flashinfer` on a B300, the server dies during warmup:

```
File ".../flashinfer/data/csrc/fmha_cutlass_sm100.cu", line 113, in FMHACutlassSM100Run
RuntimeError: Check failed: (dispatched) is false: Unsupported head dimensions: head_dim_qk=256, head_dim_vo=256
```

The MHA FlashInfer backend (`flashinfer_backend.py`) already guards against this with a supported-dims check and an FA2 fallback. The MLA backend never got the same check.

I did not find an existing issue for this.

## Modifications

- `flashinfer_backend.py`: move the CUTLASS head-dim set into a module constant, `SM100_CUTLASS_FMHA_HEAD_DIMS`. The MHA backend's behavior is unchanged.
- `flashinfer_mla_backend.py`: on SM100, use `cutlass` only when `(qk_nope + qk_rope, v_head_dim)` is in that set. Otherwise use `fa2`. Non-SM100 GPUs still use `auto`. The same `fmha_backend` also feeds the MHA chunked-prefix wrappers, so those paths are fixed too.
- DeepSeek-style models (192, 128) still use CUTLASS, as before.
- `mla/test_flashinfer.py`: new test `test_ragged_prefill_head_dims_without_cutlass_kernel`. It builds the backend for (256, 256) head dims, runs its ragged prefill wrapper, and compares the result to `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`. It fails on main on SM100 with the error above and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: 1x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (SM 10.3), driver 580.159.03, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130, flashinfer-python 0.7.2. SGLang base: `c43abd6d9e`.

Server command:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tp 1 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --mem-fraction-static 0.5 \
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --disable-radix-cache
```

Eval command (sgl-eval 0.1.3):

```bash
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:31000/v1 --num-examples 200
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| main | Server crashes during warmup (`Unsupported head dimensions: head_dim_qk=256, head_dim_vo=256`) |
| this PR | Server starts. GSM8K: 190/195 correct (97.4%), 0 request errors |

The GSM8K run stopped at 195/200. The last 5 requests were still generating long reasoning outputs when my GPU time ran out, so I stopped it. The cookbook page uses `--attention-backend triton` for this model. I used flashinfer here because that is the path this PR fixes.

Unit tests on the B300:

- `test/registered/attention/unittests/mla/test_flashinfer.py`: OK. 8 tests, 1 skipped (the existing SM10 skip on the EAGLE draft CUDA graph test).
- `test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_flashinfer.py`: OK. 8 tests.
- `test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_flashinfer.py`: OK. 8 tests.
- `test/registered/attention/unittests/hybrid_linear/test_flashinfer_mla_chunk_metadata.py`: OK. 2 tests.

I did not test on Hopper. That path still uses `auto` and is not changed.

### Known remaining limitation (not fixed here)

With the radix cache on, GLM-4.7-Flash on the FlashInfer backend still fails on requests that hit a short cached prefix. Those requests go through the absorbed MLA paged prefill. FlashInfer 0.7.2 refuses that plan when `num_heads` (20 here) does not divide the query tile:

```
fa2 MLA causal tile boundary is unsupported: request 0, num_heads=20, query=38, key=64, native KV tile=64
```

This check lives in FlashInfer (`_validate_fa_causal_tile_bound` in `mla/_batch_mla/_backends/_fa_common.py`), and it also covers the fa3 path. It is separate from the startup crash fixed here, which happens before any request is served. I think it needs a FlashInfer fix or a separate routing change in SGLang, so I left it out of this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No kernel changes. DeepSeek-style models (192, 128) keep the CUTLASS path. Models that used to crash now run on FA2, so there is no before number to compare against.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: no user-facing flag or default changed.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -124,6 +124,10 @@ def _safe_merge_state(
         return merge_state_triton(v_a, s_a, v_b, s_b)
 
 
+# (head_dim_qk, head_dim_vo) pairs FlashInfer's SM100 CUTLASS FMHA supports.
+SM100_CUTLASS_FMHA_HEAD_DIMS = frozenset({(64, 64), (128, 128), (192, 128)})
+
+
 class WrapperDispatch(Enum):
     SLIDING_WINDOW = auto()
     CROSS_ATTENTION = auto()
@@ -526,21 +530,15 @@ def __init__(
         if get_platform().is_sm100:
             fmha_backend = "fa2"
             # Disable CUTLASS backend when piecewise cuda graph is enabled
-            # due to TMA descriptor initialization issues on SM100 GPUs. The
-            # current FlashInfer SM100 CUTLASS FMHA dispatch only instantiates
-            # 64x64, 128x128, and 192x128 head dimensions. Keep unsupported
-            # shapes (for example Qwen3.5's 256x256) on the FA2 fallback.
-            cutlass_supported_head_dims = {
-                (64, 64),
-                (128, 128),
-                (192, 128),
-            }
+            # due to TMA descriptor initialization issues on SM100 GPUs. Keep
+            # shapes CUTLASS does not instantiate (for example Qwen3.5's
+            # 256x256) on the FA2 fallback.
             head_dims = (
                 model_runner.model_config.head_dim,
                 model_runner.model_config.v_head_dim,
             )
             if (
-                head_dims in cutlass_supported_head_dims
+                head_dims in SM100_CUTLASS_FMHA_HEAD_DIMS
                 and not check_cuda_graph_backend(Phase.PREFILL, Backend.TC_PIECEWISE)
             ):
                 fmha_backend = "cutlass"

@@ -30,6 +30,9 @@
 from sglang.srt.layers.attention.base_attn_backend import (
     AttentionBackend,
 )
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.flashinfer_backend import (
+    SM100_CUTLASS_FMHA_HEAD_DIMS,
+)
 from sglang.srt.layers.dcp import (
     DecodeContextParallelMetadata,
     update_local_kv_lens_for_dcp,
@@ -302,8 +305,15 @@ def __init__(
         else:
             self.q_indptr_decode = q_indptr_decode_buf
 
+        model_config = model_runner.model_config
+        ragged_head_dims = (
+            model_config.qk_nope_head_dim + model_config.qk_rope_head_dim,
+            model_config.v_head_dim,
+        )
         if get_platform().is_sm100:
-            self.fmha_backend = "cutlass"
+            self.fmha_backend = (
+                "cutlass" if ragged_head_dims in SM100_CUTLASS_FMHA_HEAD_DIMS else "fa2"
+            )
         else:
             self.fmha_backend = "auto"

@@ -1,10 +1,14 @@
 import unittest
 
 import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
 
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.flashinfer_mla_backend import FlashInferMLAAttnBackend
 from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_mode import ForwardMode
 from sglang.test.kits.attention_unittest.attention_methods.mla_attention import (
     MLAAttentionCase,
+    MockMLAModelRunner,
+    TinyMLAModelConfig,
     make_mla_cases,
     run_mla_attention_case,
 )
@@ -111,6 +115,62 @@ def test_tiny_deepseek_mla_attention_cases(self):
             with self.subTest(case=case.name, backend=case.backend):
                 run_mla_attention_case(self, case, **MLA_SHAPE_KWARGS)
 
+    def test_ragged_prefill_head_dims_without_cutlass_kernel(self):
+        """GLM-4.7-Flash style MLA (qk 256, vo 256) has no SM100 CUTLASS kernel."""
+        num_heads, num_tokens = 4, 37
+        case = MLAAttentionCase(
+            name="ragged_prefill_qk256_vo256",
+            backend="flashinfer",
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.EXTEND,
+            num_heads=num_heads,
+            page_size=1,
+            prefix_lens=(0,),
+            extend_lens=(num_tokens,),
+        )
+        model_config = TinyMLAModelConfig(
+            num_heads=num_heads,
+            kv_lora_rank=512,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+            hidden_size=1024,
+            context_len=128,
+        )
+        model_config.qk_nope_head_dim = 192
+        model_config.v_head_dim = 256
+        runner = MockMLAModelRunner(
+            case=case,
+            model_config=model_config,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            device="cuda",
+            max_context_len=128,
+            kv_lora_rank=512,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=64,
+        )
+        wrapper = FlashInferMLAAttnBackend(runner).prefill_wrapper_ragged
+
+        qo_indptr = torch.tensor([0, num_tokens], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        wrapper.begin_forward(
+            qo_indptr=qo_indptr,
+            kv_indptr=qo_indptr,
+            num_qo_heads=num_heads,
+            num_kv_heads=num_heads,
+            head_dim_qk=256,
+            head_dim_vo=256,
+            q_data_type=torch.bfloat16,
+            causal=True,
+        )
+        q, k, v = (
+            torch.randn(num_tokens, num_heads, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+            for _ in range(3)
+        )
+        out = wrapper.forward(q, k, v, causal=True, sm_scale=256**-0.5)
+        expected = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+            q.transpose(0, 1).float(),
+            k.transpose(0, 1).float(),
+            v.transpose(0, 1).float(),
+            is_causal=True,
+        ).transpose(0, 1)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), expected, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
     # Layout-robustness. See dense/test_triton.py for the full
     # rationale. FlashInfer MLA crashes with
     # `AcceleratorError: an illegal memory access was encountered`
